questions.rationale: Trauma-informed planning uses the person's experience to prevent re-traumatisation.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: Which measure is a balancing measure in a restraint-reduction project?

options.text: Staff injuries and emergency response delays.

questions.rationale: Balancing measures identify unintended effects of the intervention.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: A ward redesign reduces blind spots but also removes quiet spaces. What should leaders consider?

options.text: Whether the change increases sensory distress or escalation.

questions.rationale: Environmental safety must balance observation with trauma-informed and sensory needs.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: Which factor most strongly supports violence prevention?

options.text: Clear roles, early recognition, de-escalation and coordinated team response.

questions.rationale: Prevention depends on early and coordinated action.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: A staff member says, 'This patient always needs restraint.' What should the leader do?

options.text: Accept the judgement based on experience.
Transfer the person to another ward.
Challenge the assumption and review individual triggers, alternatives and system conditions.

questions.rationale: Normalising restriction undermines trauma-informed review and individualised care.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: A safety plan is stored in the record but unavailable during crisis. What is the primary system weakness?

options.text: The plan is not accessible and actionable when needed.
The person did not memorise it.

questions.rationale: Crisis plans must be practical and readily accessible.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: A service wants to evaluate sensory interventions. Which outcome is most relevant?

options.text: Changes in distress, restrictive practice, injuries and service-user experience.

questions.rationale: Evaluation should focus on safety, experience and actual use.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: A suicide-risk score is low, but the person has a recent loss, escalating alcohol use and access to lethal means. What should the nurse leader reinforce?

options.text: Dynamic formulation and clinical judgement should guide action.

questions.rationale: Risk formulation integrates dynamic triggers and access to means; scores do not replace judgement.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: Which review method best supports learning after an inpatient suicide attempt?

options.text: Focus only on compliance with observation policy.
Examine assessment, communication, environment, transitions and the person's experience.

questions.rationale: A systems review explores multiple interacting contributors.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: A unit reduces restraint but increases forced medication. What should leaders conclude?

options.text: Restriction may have shifted form and broader coercion data should be reviewed.

questions.rationale: Improvement should not simply substitute one restrictive practice for another.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: Which outcome best reflects purposeful observation?

options.text: Observation level is linked to current risk, engagement and regular reassessment.
The person is watched from a distance only.

questions.rationale: Observation should be therapeutic, proportionate and reviewed.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: A service has repeated aggression near medication times. What should leaders examine?

options.text: Waiting time, communication, environment, medication access and unmet needs.

questions.rationale: Patterns around time and workflow may reveal preventable triggers.

questions.sectionLabel: Reducing Restrictive Practice and Strengthening Safety Systems
questions.stem: Which outcome best demonstrates a safer mental-health system?

options.text: Restriction decreases without increased harm, and people report greater safety and dignity.

questions.rationale: Successful safety systems reduce harm while preserving dignity and protection.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: A community service identifies poor metabolic monitoring for people receiving antipsychotics. What should the improvement team do first?

options.text: Define the current gap using reliable data and map where monitoring fails.
Refer all monitoring to primary care.

questions.rationale: Quality improvement begins with a clearly defined problem and understanding of current practice.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which is an outcome measure for an integrated physical-health pathway?

options.text: Improvement in detection and follow-up of metabolic risk.

questions.rationale: Outcome measures describe the effect on health or care results.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which is a process measure for the same pathway?

options.text: Percentage of eligible people receiving weight, blood pressure, glucose and lipid monitoring.

questions.rationale: Process measures show whether recommended care occurred.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which is an experience measure?

options.text: Service users report whether physical-health care was respectful and understandable.

questions.rationale: Experience measures capture how care is perceived and whether it is acceptable.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: A project improves monitoring but creates long delays in clinic. What should leaders do?

options.text: Review the balancing measure and redesign workflow.

questions.rationale: Balancing measures help identify unintended burdens.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Why is integrated care important in mental health?

options.text: One team should control all decisions.
Physical, mental, substance-use and social needs interact and fragmented services can miss risk.
Primary care is sufficient for all needs.

questions.rationale: Integration reduces gaps and coordinates care around the person.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: A person repeatedly attends emergency care because housing instability disrupts treatment. What should the improvement plan include?

options.text: Coordination with housing and social services alongside clinical care.

questions.rationale: Social determinants directly affect mental-health outcomes and continuity.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which quality priority is most consistent with the notes?

options.text: Suicide follow-up, medication safety, physical-health monitoring and continuity of care.

questions.rationale: These are identified mental-health quality priorities.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: A service reduces readmission overall, but rates remain high for rural patients. What should leaders do?

options.text: Analyse access, transport, digital connectivity and follow-up for rural populations.

questions.rationale: Equity analysis should identify who remains excluded.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which measure set provides the strongest evaluation?

options.text: Outcome, process, experience and balancing measures.

questions.rationale: A balanced set shows effectiveness, reliability, acceptability and unintended effects.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: A project uses reminders for physical-health monitoring but completion remains low. What is the best next step?

options.text: Examine workflow, role responsibility, access and communication between services.

questions.rationale: Persistent gaps suggest system barriers beyond awareness.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which intervention best supports continuity after crisis discharge?

options.text: Advice to contact services if needed.
Clear handover, rapid follow-up, crisis plan and named responsibilities.

questions.rationale: Safe transitions require timely and coordinated follow-up.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: A service user says the new pathway is confusing. What should the team do?

options.text: Use feedback to simplify and co-design the pathway.
Explain it again using the same materials.
Remove the person from the project.

questions.rationale: Service-user experience should inform redesign.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which finding suggests diagnostic overshadowing?

options.text: A person with schizophrenia receives prompt chest-pain assessment.
Physical symptoms are attributed to mental illness without adequate examination.
Mental and physical records are linked.

questions.rationale: Diagnostic overshadowing contributes to physical-health inequality.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: A project improves physical-health checks but follow-up of abnormal results remains poor. What should leaders conclude?

options.text: The full pathway from screening to action must be redesigned.
Abnormal results are the person's responsibility.

questions.rationale: Screening alone is insufficient without reliable follow-up.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which factor should be examined when evaluating equity?

options.text: Culture, gender, age, disability, geography and socioeconomic conditions.

questions.rationale: The notes identify these dimensions for equity analysis.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: A service copies an urban intervention into a remote area and uptake is low. What is the most likely issue?

options.text: The intervention was not adapted to local resources and context.

questions.rationale: Improvement should respect local access, culture and resources.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which action best supports sustainable quality improvement?

options.text: Embedding responsibilities, workflow, feedback and ongoing measurement.

questions.rationale: Sustainability requires integration into routine systems.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: A multidisciplinary pathway has unclear ownership for abnormal results. What should leaders do?

options.text: Assign clear responsibilities and review timeframes.

questions.rationale: Integrated care requires explicit roles and accountability.

questions.sectionLabel: Quality Improvement, Integrated Care and Population Mental Health
questions.stem: Which outcome best reflects successful population mental-health improvement?

options.text: Care becomes more coordinated, outcomes improve and unequal access is reduced.

questions.rationale: Successful improvement should be effective, integrated and equitable.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: During a tele-mental health review, a person discloses an immediate suicide plan, but their exact location is unknown. What should the clinician do?

options.text: Confirm identity and location, activate the emergency plan and maintain engagement.
End the call and document it.
Ask the person to attend later.

questions.rationale: Remote care requires a clear emergency response, including identity and location confirmation.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which privacy practice is essential in tele-mental health?

options.text: Confirming privacy, identity and secure communication before sensitive discussion.
Allowing family members to remain without consent.

questions.rationale: Virtual care requires deliberate privacy and identity checks.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A mental-health app claims to predict relapse but does not explain its evidence or data use. What should leaders do?

options.text: Recommend it because it is innovative.
Use it only with younger people.
Evaluate evidence, transparency, privacy and clinical support before adoption.
Replace clinician review with the app.

questions.rationale: Digital tools should be evidence-informed, transparent and ethically integrated.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: What is algorithmic bias?

options.text: A technical error that affects everyone equally.
Systematic unfairness that may arise when predictive tools are trained on unrepresentative or biased data.

questions.rationale: Biased data can produce unequal predictions and outcomes.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A predictive tool rates a person low risk, but the clinician identifies escalating intent and access to means. What should happen?

options.text: Use professional judgement and escalate based on the clinical formulation.
Wait for the score to change.

questions.rationale: Technology supports but does not replace clinical judgement.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A rural video service improves access but excludes people without internet. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: Make video the only route to care.
Provide telephone and in-person alternatives and examine digital access barriers.
Limit the service to connected users.

questions.rationale: Digital innovation should address exclusion rather than widen it.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which feature is necessary when using telehealth in crisis-prone populations?

options.text: A tested emergency escalation plan and awareness of what cannot be assessed remotely.

questions.rationale: Remote care must plan for emergencies and clinical limitations.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A service uses online peer support. What should leaders consider?

options.text: Moderation, evidence, privacy, escalation pathways and integration with clinical support.

questions.rationale: Online support should be safe, transparent and connected to appropriate care.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A digital tool recommends a diagnosis based on limited self-report data. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Treat the result as one source of information and complete a broader assessment.
Tell the person the tool is definitive.

questions.rationale: Digital outputs should be interpreted within comprehensive clinical assessment.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which measure best evaluates digital equity?

options.text: Access and outcomes by geography, age, disability, language and socioeconomic status.

questions.rationale: Disaggregated data reveal who benefits and who remains excluded.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A virtual consultation takes place while family members can overhear. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Continue because the person joined the call.
Ask the family to listen quietly.
Check whether the person has privacy and arrange an alternative if needed.

questions.rationale: Privacy must be actively assessed in remote care.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A digital service experiences a platform failure during a crisis call. What should be available?

options.text: A tested backup communication and emergency pathway.

questions.rationale: Downtime and backup planning are essential for safety.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A global programme proposes copying a high-income digital model into a low-resource setting. What should leaders do?

options.text: Adapt it to local culture, infrastructure, workforce and community priorities.

questions.rationale: Global collaboration should respect local knowledge and resources.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which statement best reflects ethical digital mental-health practice?

options.text: Digital tools should support access while preserving privacy, judgement, transparency and choice.
Algorithms are more objective than clinicians.
Online care is suitable for every situation.

questions.rationale: Technology should augment, not replace, humane and accountable care.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A predictive model performs less accurately for one cultural group. What should leaders do?

options.text: Continue because overall accuracy is acceptable.
Exclude that group from the service.
Investigate bias, involve affected communities and reconsider use until safety is addressed.
Train clinicians to trust the model.

questions.rationale: Unequal model performance creates safety and equity concerns.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which global mental-health initiative is most sustainable?

options.text: A programme dependent on external experts.
A locally co-designed service that builds workforce capability and uses available resources.

questions.rationale: Sustainability requires local relevance, ownership and capacity.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: An app sends alarming notifications without access to clinical support. What is the main concern?

options.text: The tool may increase distress without a safe response pathway.

questions.rationale: Digital tools should include appropriate support and escalation.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which outcome best demonstrates successful tele-mental health implementation?

options.text: Access improves without compromising privacy, emergency response, therapeutic quality or equity.

questions.rationale: Success requires safety, quality and equitable access, not volume alone.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: How should Global Nursing Professionals use international evidence?

options.text: Critically appraise and adapt learning to local culture, resources and service-user priorities.

questions.rationale: Global learning should be adapted respectfully and sustainably.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Mental Health and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which outcome best reflects Level 3 digital and global practice?

options.text: Technology is used critically, exclusion is addressed and global learning strengthens culturally relevant care.

questions.rationale: Level 3 practice combines ethical technology use, equity and adapted global collaboration.
